description: The British Columbia groundwater-levels-indicator repository contains R code for calculating long-term groundwater trends. Its README says it draws on the province's Observation Well Network and the bcgroundwater package, producing provincial and individual-well summaries and graphics for an environmental indicator. Users choose wells and an observation period; outputs are trend measures for the included records. Geographic coverage is British Columbia, Canada. GitHub metadata states Apache-2.0 licensing for the code; source monitoring data keep their government data terms. A limitation is that trend estimates depend on observation continuity, well siting and pumping history, and do not directly predict future aquifer storage. The workflow can calibrate groundwater stress assumptions for water-supply, agricultural or drought simulations. The related EPANET catalogue model addresses distribution pipes, not aquifer monitoring. No well records or R package were downloaded.
name: BC groundwater-level trend workflow
